diag.client_error_hint: The gateway or the provider refused the request as sent: a parameter, a size or a format.
diag.approval_hint: A policy asked a person to approve a tool or an answer before it went on.
diag.tool_errors_hint: The model got an error back from these tools. A failed tool's text is sealed; its kind is in the timeline.
diag.truncated: The answer was cut off at {{tokens}} tokens

diag.filtered_hint: The provider's content filter stopped the answer.
diag.slow_first_token_hint: The time to the first token is queueing plus reading the prompt. A long wait points to a busy runtime or a very long prompt.
diag.slow_generation_hint: The model wrote slowly once it had started. The runtime may be overloaded, or its GPU shared with other work.
diag.outlier: Slower than most: {{latency}} against a p95 of {{p95}}
diag.outlier_hint: This call took far longer than 95% of the calls shown. Compare its tokens and its provider with faster ones.
diag.no_usage: The provider reported no token usage

diag.retried_hint: The gateway tried again after a failure; the latency includes every attempt.

hf_access.title: Hugging Face access
hf_access.why: Models come from Hugging Face. Public models need no token. Gated ones (Llama, Gemma and some Mistral models) need a token from an account that has accepted their license, and a token also raises download limits.

hf_access.storage_unsafe: This server still uses the default settings master key, so a saved token would not be protected. Set FADEN_BACKEND_SETTINGS_MASTER_KEY to a random value and restart before saving one.
hf_access.security_note: Stored encrypted on this server and never shown again, not even to administrators. Only this server uses it: cluster machines get their models from this server, not from Hugging Face. A container on this server started with remote code allowed is given the token and keeps it until it is stopped and started again.

blurb.tiny_verified: The smallest useful chat model, tested on this setup: the quickest way to see a deployment work end to end.
blurb.tiny: Tiny and fast: for trying things out rather than real work.
blurb.small_capable: Small but capable: runs almost anywhere and handles everyday chat and simple tool use.
blurb.all_rounder: A strong all-rounder that fits comfortably on one accelerator.
blurb.stronger: Noticeably better answers than the 8B models, for more memory.
blurb.gpt_oss_small: OpenAI's open-weight model: strong reasoning and tool use at a modest size.
blurb.moe_fast: Mixture of experts: a large model's knowledge at the speed of a small one.
blurb.flagship: Qwen's current flagship dense model: strong at chat, tools and reasoning. At full precision it needs a lot of accelerator memory.
blurb.flagship_fp8: The flagship stored in 8 bits (FP8): about half the memory, almost the same quality.
blurb.coder_large: A large mixture-of-experts model for agentic coding; needs plenty of accelerator memory.
blurb.mistral_small: Mistral's small model: good at following instructions, tools and European languages.
blurb.gpt_oss_large: OpenAI's large open-weight model: near-frontier reasoning; needs a large accelerator or several.
blurb.large_dense: A large dense model: very capable, and needs plenty of accelerator memory.
blurb.coder: Built for code: completion, explanation and agentic coding tools.
blurb.reasoning: Thinks step by step before answering: better at maths and logic, slower to reply.
blurb.vision: Reads images and documents as well as text.
blurb.gemma: Google's open model: strong multilingual chat that also understands images.
blurb.embedding_small: A small, fast embedding model for search and knowledge bases.
blurb.embedding_large: A large embedding model: better retrieval, more memory.
blurb.images_turbo: Pictures in a few seconds from a 6B model under Apache-2.0: photos, illustrations and legible text in pictures.
blurb.images_large: A larger picture model under Apache-2.0: four steps, more memory.
